meanings.note: Contrast. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.
Starting a question: а жвачку?. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
ends a conversation or an order: 'Всё, свободен' = that's all, you can go
At the start of a sentence. Core Russian pron meaning 'everything, all; that's it' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('stupid, silly, foolish').

examples.text: Ваня, ты глупый? Зачем ты сейчас это при нём сказал?
examples.trans: Vanya, are you stupid? Why did you just say that in front of him?

meanings.en: dwarf, gnome (mythological creature or mocking word for a short person)
meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'dwarf, gnome' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Who's a dwarf? I'm a dwarf?
Seven dwarfs lived in the fairy tale.
Listen here, you dwarf! Go away from here.

meanings.note: давай + 1st person plural or infinitive
давай + 1st person plural or infinitive

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: думать о + prepositional = to think about

examples.trans: I have no time to think about that.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Colloquial reproach. Common masculine noun meaning 'fool, idiot' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Костик, ты дурак! Это статусная вещь.
examples.trans: Kostik, you're a fool! This is a status piece.

meanings.note: Запись идёт = it is recording. Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'пись'). Common feminine noun meaning 'recording; entry, appointment' in everyday Russian.
Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'пись'). Common feminine noun meaning 'recording; entry, appointment' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I listened to the recording of the conversation.

examples.text: Кто здесь снимает? Кто оператор? Запись идёт?
examples.trans: Who is filming here? Who is the cameraman? Is it recording?

meanings.note: Location. Core Russian adv meaning 'here' in everyday speech.
emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: In one direction, now. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go (on foot)', paired with 'пойти'.
To run for a second term. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go (on foot)', paired with 'пойти'.

examples.trans: He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'book' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: He is reading an interesting book.
Samsonov, here, please, is your book.

meanings.note: everyday affectionate word for книга
Трудовая книжка, зачётная книжка. Common feminine noun meaning 'book (colloquial/diminutive); booklet' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: She is reading a children's book.

examples.text: Надо пить меньше. Книжки буду читать.
examples.trans: I need to drink less. I'm going to read books.

meanings.note: the 'е' drops out in the other forms
Radio and phone phrase. Common masculine noun meaning 'end' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: At the end of the film everyone is happy.

meanings.note: in the instrumental: 'кем ты работаешь?'

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: Там мелко = It's shallow there. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: What do you mean drowning? It's shallow there!
Near the shore it is very shallow.

examples.text: А чего тону? Там мелко! Сиди!
examples.trans: What do you mean drowning? It's shallow there! Stay put!

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
usually in the genitive ничего, with не: ничего не осталось

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence
Ну, папа!. Core Russian part meaning 'well; come on' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Borrowed from Latin agent/instrument noun in '-tor' ('оператор'). Common masculine noun meaning 'cameraman, operator' in everyday Russian.
Borrowed from Latin agent/instrument noun in '-tor' ('оператор'). Common masculine noun meaning 'cameraman, operator' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Who is filming here? Who is the cameraman?
The cameraman turned on the camera.

examples.text: Кто здесь снимает? Кто оператор? Запись идёт?
examples.trans: Who is filming here? Who is the cameraman? Is it recording?

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'from; of' in everyday speech.
Тошнит от = sick of. Core Russian prep meaning 'from; of' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.en: to give away, to hand over
meanings.note: Отдать + dative of the person. Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'дать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to give (away), to hand over', paired with 'отдавать'.

Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'дать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to give (away), to hand over', paired with 'отдавать'.

examples.trans: He will hand over the money.

examples.text: Потом надо отдать москвичам твои деньги из подвала.
examples.trans: Then I have to give your money from the basement to the Moscow people.

meanings.note: Locative / directional adverb. Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'сюда').

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: + dative. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мочь'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to help', paired with 'помогать'.

examples.text: Экскаваторщик — это не мой уровень. Может, поможешь?
examples.trans: Excavator driver isn't my level. Maybe you could help?

meanings.note: Понял? = got it?; понял = got it. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to understand', paired with 'понимать'.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Borrowed from Latin agent/instrument noun in '-tor' ('провокатор'). Common masculine noun meaning 'provocateur, instigator' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Are you a provocateur from Osipenko?
Sonny, are you a provocateur from Osipenko?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'делать'.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'емья'). Common feminine noun meaning 'family' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Так, семья Самсоновых. Он строитель, она медсестра.
examples.trans: Right, the Samsonov family. He's a builder, she's a nurse.

meanings.note: Informal. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'идеть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to sit, to be sitting', paired with 'посидеть'.

examples.trans: Why are you sitting in the corner?

meanings.note: Слышать о + prepositional. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лышать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to hear', paired with 'услышать'.

Слышать о + prepositional. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лышать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to hear', paired with 'услышать'.

examples.text: Как странно, я ничего об этом не слышал.
examples.trans: How strange, I've heard nothing about it.

снимать.gloss: to take off; to film; to rent

meanings.note: Clothes, a ring. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'нимать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to take off; to film; to rent', paired with 'снять'.

Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'нимать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to take off; to film; to rent', paired with 'снять'.

Снимать квартиру. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'нимать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to take off; to film; to rent', paired with 'снять'.

examples.trans: Watch. I'm taking off my ring.

сыночек.gloss: sonny, little son (affectionate diminutive of сын)

meanings.en: sonny, little son (affectionate or ironic diminutive of сын)
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ыночек'). Common masculine noun meaning 'sonny, little son (affectionate diminutive of сын)' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Sonny, are you a provocateur from Osipenko?

meanings.note: Direction. Core Russian adv meaning 'here (to this place)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The white one? Give me the keys.

meanings.note: 'что я за мэр такой' = what kind of mayor am I
Core Russian pron meaning 'such, like this' in everyday speech.
там такие деньги = there's so much money in it

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: the comparative 'тише' = quieter, used as 'shh'
тише! (comparative) = quiet! keep it down!

meanings.en: to drown, to be drowning, to sink
meanings.note: Present: тону, тонешь, тонет. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to drown, to sink', paired with 'утонуть'.

examples.trans: The ship began to sink slowly.

examples.text: А чего тону? Там мелко! Сиди!
examples.trans: What do you mean drowning? It's shallow there! Stay put!

meanings.note: Colloquial, like здесь. Core Russian adv meaning 'here' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: irregular mixed conjugation: убегу, убежишь, ..., убегут

examples.trans: The dog ran away into the courtyard.

examples.text: Всё, убежал! Тут уже ничего не сделать.
examples.trans: That's it, he ran away! Nothing can be done here now.

meanings.en: to hit, to strike, to punch
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'дарить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to hit, to strike', paired with 'ударять'.

examples.trans: He struck the table with his fist.

examples.text: Вот если бы он ребёнка ударил!
examples.trans: Now if he had hit a child!

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Conjunction. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'I' in everyday speech.
Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good, nice').

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.
